hook.text: Even asteroids have moons. Over 400 asteroids are known to have one or more tiny companions orbiting them.

buildup.text: Dactyl was the first asteroid moon discovered in 1993, orbiting the asteroid Ida. Galileo snapped the image during a flyby.

discovery.text: Asteroid Dinkinesh, visited by Lucy in 2023, surprised everyone with a contact-binary moon—two tiny rocks touching.

twist.text: Asteroid moons form from collisions, spin-off, or gravitational capture. Some binary asteroids spin so fast they nearly fly apart.

climax.text: DART proved we can deflect asteroids by hitting Dimorphos—the moon of asteroid Didymos. Planetary defense works.

punchline.text: Even rocks have moons. We've already redirected one for planetary defense.

quiz.question: What did NASA's DART mission accomplish at the asteroid Didymos?
options: It successfully deflected the asteroid's moon Dimorphos, proving planetary defense is possible
It landed on the asteroid and collected samples for return to Earth
It discovered that the asteroid had water ice on its surface

details.summary: Many asteroids have their own tiny moons. Over 400 asteroid binaries and triples are known, with companion objects ranging from boulders to substantial satellites. The first confirmed asteroid moon was Dactyl, orbiting asteroid Ida, photographed by the Galileo spacecraft in 1993.
details.whyItMatters: Asteroid moons reveal asteroid internal structure, density, and composition — critical information for both planetary science and planetary defense efforts to deflect potentially hazardous asteroids.
takeaways: Over 400 asteroids known to have one or more moons
Form through collisions, spin-up fission, or tidal effects
Key to determining asteroid mass and internal structure

faq.question: How do asteroids get moons?
faq.answer: Impacts can eject debris that settles into orbit. The YORP effect (uneven solar heating) can spin asteroids until they break apart, with fragments entering orbit. Tidal forces during close planetary flybys can also split asteroids.

faq.question: Why are asteroid moons important for planetary defense?
faq.answer: NASA's DART mission successfully deflected Dimorphos, the moon of asteroid Didymos, in 2022 — the first planetary defense test.
